surface_v1_deprecated: --surface {surface} publishes the v1 tools. They are deprecated and are removed in 0.11.0. Move to the v2 tools: agentless-mcp guide --section the-two-surfaces has the mapping.
server_no_roots: no repositories are served: this server was started with no roots. Roots come from --root DIR flags and from --roots-from FILE, which lists one repository path per line. A root advertised by the client can only select among the roots the server is configured with; it cannot add one.
server_root_required: repo_root is required: this server holds several repositories and will not guess between them. Retry with repo_root set to one of: {roots}
unknown_operation: {tool} has no operation named '{operation}'. Valid operations are: {operations}. Retry with one of those.
op_rejects_parameters: {tool} operation '{operation}' does not accept: {stray}. This operation accepts: {accepted}; required: {required}. Drop the stray parameters, or pick the operation that takes them.
op_requires_parameters: {tool} operation '{operation}' is missing: {missing}. This operation accepts: {accepted}; required: {required}. Retry naming the missing parameters.
path_needs_endpoints: {tool} operation 'path' needs both source and target: each is a stable id, a qualified name, or a repository-relative file path. Retry naming both ends.
map_limit_out_of_range: orient operation 'map' rejects limit={limit}: the map's file cap runs {minimum}-{maximum}, which is the same bound repo_map publishes as max_files. The wider ceiling on this parameter belongs to the communities and cycles listings that share it. Retry with a limit in range.
repo_refused_no_roots: repository refused: this server was started with no roots, so it serves no repositories. Roots come from --root DIR flags and from --roots-from FILE, which lists one repository path per line.
repo_refused_not_allowed: repository refused: the requested root is not one of this server's roots. Retry with repo_root set to one of: {roots}
roots_file_hint: To serve another repository, append its absolute path as a line in {file}; the file is re-read on the next call, no restart needed.
roots_file_unreadable: roots file {file} cannot be read: {error}. Refusing rather than serving the stale copy; restore the file, or restart the server without --roots-from.
map_unresolved_seeds: // note: these focus seeds matched no file, no symbol, and no name spelled in five or fewer non-test files of this repository, so the ranking below is not focused on them: {seeds}. Check the spelling, or seed with a file path from the tree.
scan_skipped_files: // warning: {count} files were skipped and are absent from this answer: {listed}. A symbol in a skipped file reads as missing here even though it may exist in the repository.
find_no_matches: no matching symbols: no declared symbol has '{query}' in its name or qualified name, matched case-insensitively. A parameter, a local variable, an attribute or a string literal is not a declared symbol; grep for the literal to find those.
find_unparsed: note: {query} is spelled where a file did not parse ({listed}), so a declaration there may be missing from this answer
find_no_matches_kind: no matching symbols of kind '{kind}': '{query}' does match symbols of other kinds: {kinds}. Retry with one of those kinds, or with no kind.
find_data_folded: {path}: {count} data keys match. Grep finds the spellings.
find_data_unlisted: {count} data keys in {total} files match and are not listed: {listed}. Grep finds the spellings.
find_data_not_symbols: Keys below depth 2 and keys in lists of JSON, TOML and YAML files are not symbols. Grep finds them.
overview_data_unlisted: {count} more keys are not listed: the outline stops at depth 2, at list items and at {cap} keys. Grep finds them.
span_data_key_unlisted: {path} keeps an outline of its keys, and {qualname} is not in it: the outline stops at depth 2, at list items and at {cap} keys. Read the lines with read slice, or Grep for the key.
expand_body_truncated: ... {shown} of {total} lines shown: the batch did not fit the output ceiling. Expand this id on its own for the whole body.
expand_batch_shortened: note: {shortened} of {total} bodies were shortened to fit the {budget}-token expansion budget; every requested id still appears, each marked where it was cut. Expand fewer ids per call for whole bodies.
expand_no_room: not expanded: {requested} ids exceed the {seats} one call can answer; retry with at most that many.
map_file_unreached: ... {count} symbols in this file; the focus has no reference path to it, so no budget shows them
refs_target_unresolved: {target} resolves to no symbol; these are the references to the name {name}, wherever it is defined
explain_tie: ambiguous: {count} definitions match {target} equally; this explains the first in path order. Pass a stable id to explain another.
communities_not_converged: note: community detection stopped at its pass limit before the partition settled, so these communities are a partial answer
overview_stable_ids: stable ids: {pattern} -- nested symbols qualify as Class.method
slice_range_beyond_file: unsatisfiable: line range {start}-{end} is beyond {path} ({total} lines)
slice_range_not_a_range: unsatisfiable: line range {start}-{end} is not a range in {path}: a start of 1 or more, and an end at or after the start
cache_stale_remediation: changed files parse live; run agentless-mcp index --repo {repo_root} for performance
cache_stale_refreshing: changed files parse live; a background refresh is in progress
cache_absent_refreshing: a background refresh is in progress
cache_build_hint: tag cache is empty: parsing is on demand; run agentless-mcp index --repo {repo_root} to build it
cache_discarded_no_index: cache discarded: no index has been built
cache_discarded_old_schema: cache discarded: schema {found} predates {expected}, rerun agentless-mcp index
cache_discarded_other_repo: cache discarded: it was built for {repo_root}
history_target_unresolved: {target}: {reason}. Pass a stable id from a map, overview, find, explain or locate answer; history is span-scoped, so a bare name is refused.
history_path_not_in_head: unsatisfiable: {path} is not in HEAD (untracked, ignored, or only staged). Commit it, or ask about a tracked file.
history_span_beyond_head: unsatisfiable: lines {start}-{end} of {path} are past the end of HEAD's copy. The working tree grew the file since the last commit; commit, then ask again.
history_git_output_malformed: git printed log output history cannot read: {detail}. history refuses a partial read rather than answer from one. Check that this git honours --no-patch together with -L, and that no filter rewrites git log output.
history_more_commits: ... {shown} newest commits shown; older commits touch this span (raise limit for the rest)
history_seats_capped: ... {shown} commits shown, the most one answer seats; older commits touch this span (ask about a narrower span, or run git log -L{start},{end}:{path} for the rest)
history_body_truncated: ... {shown} of {total} body lines shown for {sha}; git show -s --format=%B {sha} prints the whole message
history_output_capped: ... git output was cut at {bytes} bytes; the {count} complete commits above are shown
history_output_capped_no_commits: unsatisfiable: git output reached the {bytes} byte cap before the first complete commit. The newest commit on lines {start}-{end} of {path} carries a message larger than the cap; run git log -L{start},{end}:{path} to read it.
history_dirty_file: note: {path} has uncommitted changes; the span was located in the committed copy of the file (lines {start}-{end} there), so these commits follow the committed definition
history_dirty_unknown: note: git could not say whether {path} has uncommitted changes ({note}); the span was located in the committed copy of the file (lines {start}-{end} there)
history_symbol_not_in_head: unsatisfiable: {name} is not defined in the committed copy of {path}: it is new or renamed in the working tree, so no commit has touched it yet
history_signature_changed: note: {name} has a different signature in the committed copy than in the working tree; these commits follow the committed definition
history_shallow: note: this clone is shallow, so the oldest commit listed may stand in for older history
history_shallow_unknown: note: git could not say whether this clone is shallow ({note}); in a shallow clone the oldest commit listed may stand in for older history
complexity_language_unsupported: {path}: complexity has no rules for language '{language}'. It measures only these languages: {languages}.
complexity_does_not_parse: {path} does not parse: the first syntax error is at line {line}. Complexity is measured only for a file that parses. Fix the syntax error, then measure the file again.
complexity_tokenizer_rejects: {path}: Python's tokenizer rejects this file ({detail}). Complexity is measured only for a file the tokenizer accepts, the same as scb-check. Fix the line the error names, then measure the file again.
complexity_grew: {qualname}: complexity {old_cc} -> {new_cc}, {old_sloc} -> {new_sloc} source lines. This function is already above the threshold ({threshold}), and this change adds more branching to it. Put the new branches in a new named function and call it, or refactor this function first in its own change.
complexity_crossed: {qualname}: complexity {old_cc} -> {new_cc}, {old_sloc} -> {new_sloc} source lines. This change takes the function over the threshold ({threshold}). Put the new branches in a new named function and call it, or refactor this function first in its own change.
complexity_new_unit: {qualname}: complexity {new_cc}, {new_sloc} source lines. This function is new, or moved from another file, and it is above the threshold ({threshold}). Split it into smaller named functions. If it moved here unchanged, it was already above the threshold in its old file.
complexity_old_not_measured: not checked: complexity_delta did not compare {path}, because its text before the change cannot be measured. {reason}
complexity_new_not_measured: not checked: complexity_delta did not compare {path}, because its text after the change cannot be measured. {reason}
pair_old_unread: not checked: the text of {path} before the change was not read ({reason}), so no pair check compared this file.
pair_new_unread: not checked: the proposed text for {path} was not read ({reason}), so no pair check compared this file.
pair_edits_unapplied: not checked: {failed} of the edits to {path} did not apply, so no pair check compared this file.
lint_no_checks: no check selected. Name at least one of these checks: {checks}.
lint_path_needs_after: --path and --after go together: --path names the file in --repo, and --after names a file that holds its proposed new text.
lint_path_takes_pair_checks: --path runs only the pair checks ({pair_checks}), because it supplies whole-file text and no patch. Remove {checks} from --only, or lint a patch with --candidates or --diff.
lint_since_alone: --since takes no --after. --since compares each file changed since REV with its text in the working tree, so it needs no other input.
lint_since_takes_pair_checks: --since runs only the pair checks ({pair_checks}), because the other checks compare a patch with the current tree and would see two states mixed. Remove {checks} from --only.
lint_revision_unresolved: --since {revision} does not name a commit in this repository ({note}). Name a commit, for example --since "$(git merge-base HEAD main)".
lint_revision_not_resolved: not checked: git did not resolve --since {revision} ({note}), so no pair check compared any file.
lint_revision_unlisted: not checked: git {command} did not list the changed files ({note}), so no pair check compared any file.
lint_revision_listing_capped: not checked: git {command} printed more than {bytes} bytes, so the list of changed files is not complete and no pair check compared any file. Review a shorter range of commits.
lint_revision_output_malformed: git printed output that the review cannot read: {detail}.
lint_revision_unchanged: not checked: no file changed since {revision}, so there is nothing to compare.
lint_revision_submodule: not checked: {path} is a submodule. The pair checks read only the files of this repository.
lint_revision_binary: not checked: {path} is binary, so no pair check compared this file.
lint_revision_binary_evidence: a NUL byte in the first {bytes} bytes
lint_revision_status: not checked: git reports {path} with status {status}, for example an unresolved merge conflict, so no pair check compared this file.
pair_worktree_unread: not checked: the working-tree text of {path} was not read ({reason}), so no pair check compared this file.
pair_blob_over_cap: skipped: the committed text exceeds the per-file cap of {cap} bytes
config_erosion_gate_not_object: erosion_gate in {config} must be an object that maps a check name to one of {modes}. The key is ignored.
config_erosion_gate_mode: erosion_gate.{check} in {config} must be one of {modes}. The entry is ignored.
config_erosion_gate_unknown: erosion_gate in {config} holds {count} entries that name no gated check ({checks}). They are ignored.
contract_no_boundary: not checked: contract_drift has no boundary modules to check. Set boundary_globs in {config} to the globs of the modules that parse foreign data.
contract_no_rules: not checked: contract_drift has no rules for {language}, so it did not check {path}.
contract_old_not_measured: not checked: contract_drift did not compare {path}, because its text before the change cannot be measured. {reason}
contract_new_not_measured: not checked: contract_drift did not compare {path}, because its text after the change cannot be measured. {reason}
contract_new_hit: {unit}: {capture} is new in a boundary module ({rule}). {why}
clone_language_unsupported: {path}: clone blocks have no rules for language '{language}'. They are indexed only in these languages: {languages}.
clone_does_not_parse: {path} does not parse: the first syntax error is at line {line}. Clone blocks are indexed only in a file that parses. Fix the syntax error, then index the file again.
clone_tokenizer_rejects: {path}: Python's tokenizer rejects this file ({detail}). Clone blocks are indexed only in a file the tokenizer accepts, the same as scb-check. Fix the line the error names, then index the file again.
clone_old_not_indexed: not checked: clone_delta did not compare {path}, because its text before the change cannot be indexed. {reason}
clone_new_not_indexed: not checked: clone_delta did not compare {path}, because its text after the change cannot be indexed. {reason}
clone_index_gaps: not checked: clone_delta did not index {count} of {total} repository files, so it does not see a copy of a block in them: {paths}.
clone_index_unlisted: not checked: clone_delta could not list the repository files ({reason}), so it compared the changed files only with each other.
clone_index_stopped: stopped: the clone index reached its time budget before this file
clone_no_tag_cache: not checked: in the hook form, clone_delta reads the repository's clone blocks from the tag cache only, and this run has no tag cache. Run agentless-mcp index on the repository to turn the check on.
clone_new_copy: lines {start}-{end} add a copy of a block, with names and literals ignored, and this repository now holds {count} copies of it. Each copy must be changed with the others. Move the shared code into one named function, and call it from each place.
config_boundary_globs_not_list: boundary_globs in {config} must be a list of at most {limit} repo-relative globs, each at most {chars} characters. The key is ignored.
config_boundary_globs_too_many: boundary_globs in {config} holds {count} globs, over the {limit} cap. The key is ignored.
config_boundary_globs_dropped: boundary_globs in {config}: {count} entries are not repo-relative globs of at most {chars} characters. They are ignored.
